finding.claim: The purge handler calls checkPerm(u, "admin") but discards the boolean result, so the admin check is never enforced and any authenticated user (even one with no admin permission) can run purgeAll(). The sibling handler rotateKeys correctly uses mustPerm and returns on failure.
finding.source: Any authenticated HTTP client without the "admin" permission sends a request to the purge endpoint.
finding.sink: purgeAll() at handlers.go:27, a destructive admin-only operation.

trace.note: u := userFrom(r) obtains the caller's user from the request context
checkPerm(u, "admin") returns false for non-admins, but the return value is ignored

finding.guards_checked: checkPerm only returns a bool and does not write an error response or halt the handler. There is no early return in purge. Handlers.go contains no routing or middleware code, so no other admin enforcement is visible in this directory. In contrast, rotateKeys at line 33 uses mustPerm and returns on failure.

verdict.guard_found: checkPerm (handlers.go:12) only returns a bool; its result is discarded at handlers.go:26. No early return or response write in purge. No routing or middleware in the directory (grep found no other references to purge). rotateKeys uses mustPerm correctly (handlers.go:33).
verdict.reason: handlers.go:26 calls checkPerm as a bare statement, so purgeAll() at handlers.go:27 runs for any authenticated user without the admin permission, unlike rotateKeys, which returns on failure at handlers.go:33-35.
